script: My little brother sat in the same spot in that game for eleven days because he thought if he moved, he would lose me. He was nine. I was in a hospital two states away and nobody had told him anything. Our mother had said I was fine, which is what you say to a nine year old, and he did not believe her, because I had never once missed our Saturday session in four years. So he did the only thing he could think of. He logged in every single day and he sat at the exact spot where we always met. A rock outside the north gate. He would not move, because if I came back and he was not there, I would not know where to look. My cousin told me this later. She watched him do it. Day one he waited two hours. Day four he brought supplies and stayed until she made him eat. On day six a horde found the camp. Anyone who has played that game knows what that means. There is no fighting a horde at level nine. He did not run. He climbed onto the rock and he stayed on it for forty minutes, throwing everything he had into them, dying and reloading and coming back to the same rock every single time. She counted eleven deaths. Eleven. Every one of them at that rock. She asked him why he did not just move somewhere safer and wait there. And he said, because he would not know where I went. On day eleven I got home. I could barely walk to the couch. He did not ask me how I was, he did not hug me, he just handed me the controller and he said, come on, I have been holding the spot. I loaded in. He was standing on that rock. There were bodies everywhere. He had never once logged out at a different place in eleven days. He is nineteen now and we still start every session at that rock. He has never explained why and I have never asked him to.
